A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POLICYGUARDBENCH and POLICYGUARD-4B work despite retitling and reformatting. All pages and appendices are readable, and the methods, tables, equations, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark, prefix-detection, cross-domain generalization, and inference-efficiency results in Tables 2–5 and appendix plots.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds human re-annotation, closed-loop agent simulation, and error-analysis findings.

M1.justification: The Qwen3-4B backbone, supervised fine-tuning, inputs, and binary classification formulation remain unchanged. Appendix C adds a limited procedural extension: screening proposed actions before execution, blocking detected violations, and triggering retries.

E1.justification: The five-domain WebArena-derived benchmark and full-trajectory, prefix, and held-out-domain coverage remain unchanged. Appendix C adds an interactive closed-loop web-agent scenario that evaluates policy-compliant task execution beyond offline classification; no additional named dataset or domain is introduced.

E2.justification: The named comparator sets in Tables 2, 3, and 5 are unchanged after matching abbreviated model names. Appendix C adds a comparison against an agent without guardrail intervention, although that agent's backbone is unspecified.

E3.justification: v2 substantially broadens evaluation design with an independent 287-pair human audit and a controlled closed-loop comparison measuring Completion-Under-Policy, violation blocking, and session overhead. Section 3.2 also specifies trajectory isolation, but describes it as both standard and additional; this does not establish that the retained experiments were rerun under a changed split.

E4.justification: v2 adds label-reliability validation, an intervention study, and detailed error analysis by error type, trajectory length, domain, and failure mechanism, including manual inspection of 100 errors. These address substantial validation questions absent from v1. Existing prefix and leave-one-domain-out analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain seed 42 and deterministic decoding, without repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new human-agreement percentage and error rates are additional point results rather than a changed uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and the prefix plots retain their numerical results. Substantial additional findings include 89.8% human-label agreement, closed-loop CuP of 10.20% without intervention versus 16.33% with intervention, a 71.97% violation-block rate, 26.8 ms per online guardrail call, and Table 7's error breakdowns. These are newly reported analyses, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The Efficiency-Adjusted F1 definition and normalization in Section 4.5 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a policy-compliance benchmark, prefix-based detection, and an efficient 4B guardrail with cross-domain generalization. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain these substantive claims; the new studies provide additional supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 removes v1's explicit compliant-prefix class-prior caveat and emphasizes early directional intent and benign-action noise. v2 also expands the argument against synthesis-artifact explanations, attributes errors to interface-grounding difficulties, and adds substantive limitations concerning missing visual context and untested domains beyond WebArena-style environments.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents partitioning by the 733 base trajectories and updates the project-page access pointer. It removes v1's explicit commitment to release code, data, and checkpoints. The optimization settings in Table 6 and existing hardware and decoding disclosures remain unchanged; actual resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds background citations covering Constitutional AI, shielding, safe reinforcement learning, over-refusal, evaluation, and recent safeguards. The central positioning of policy compliance as distinct from conventional safety remains unchanged. The gpt-oss citation's change from OpenAI to Agarwal et al. refers to the same work.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, rewrites the abstract and selected paragraphs, and reorganizes the appendices. Ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements are replaced by impact, limitations, and acknowledgement sections. Most main-section ordering and explanatory prose remain recognizable and unchanged.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference-format main text and bibliography, with extensive table restyling and figure resizing and repositioning. Figure 2 moves from the appendix into the main text, and Table 7 is added. Existing figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The human-label audit, downstream intervention check, and concrete error and applicability analyses provide useful validation and qualification absent from v1. Gains are limited by missing simulation agent/sample details and ambiguous split descriptions. Table 7's 1,091 errors among 12,000 examples also imply 90.91% accuracy, conflicting with Table 2's retained 90.14%. Removing the prefix class-prior caveat weakens interpretive balance. Overall, the additions improve the paper modestly without establishing a substantial reliability improvement.
